baseline-sl7.concurrency_test: Paused catalog commit permits reads of the affected and unrelated inodes and native writes to another inode; conflicting mutations wait; release/forget pins survive through reply capture.
baseline-sl7.durability: Namespace timestamp commits use WAL/NORMAL; file and directory fsync perform a nonempty FULL catalog transaction before native sync; content publication remains FULL
baseline-sl7.barrier_tests: FULL mode enforced by SQL trigger; file/directory/datasync boundaries; injected failure propagation and reservation release; sealed namespace metadata survives daemon kill after fsync

retirement.concurrency_test: Paused catalog commit permits reads of the affected and unrelated inodes and native writes to another inode; conflicting mutations wait; release/forget pins survive through reply capture.
retirement.durability: Content manifest and binding remain FULL-durable before native retirement. The catalog permit is released after binding; the inode gate excludes mutations until retirement completes. Timestamp sync policy is unchanged.
retirement.retirement_test: Paused retirement blocks same-inode writes and hardlinks while another sealed inode hydrates, writes, and fsyncs; both mutation paths are observed waiting at the inode gate.

sl7.concurrency_test: Paused catalog commit permits reads of the affected and unrelated inodes and native writes to another inode; conflicting mutations wait; release/forget pins survive through reply capture.
sl7.durability: Manifest and live binding commit atomically in one FULL transaction before native retirement. Timestamp sync policy and inode gates are unchanged.
sl7.atomic_seal_test: Binding failure rolls back manifest and chunks; process death after manifest insertion but before binding/commit preserves native bytes with an empty catalog; post-commit recovery still reconstructs exact bytes.

limitations: Two rounds on a shared node; no claim of statistical significance.
Post-build CPU-idle observation does not establish a drained sealing queue.
Warm OS caches; no release rerun.
Namespace timestamp sync policy is unchanged; content mappings retain FULL durability.
